paragraphs.text: Linear tools and hosted MCP bridge for DeepSeek Harness
# @kb1slnlabs/dsh-linear
**Getting started:** Install in DSH Desktop.

Linear issue-tracking tools for the DeepSeek Harness. A Cordis function/namespace
plugin (`export {

name, inject, apply }`, no default export) that registers
model-facing tools through `ctx.tools.regi

inject, apply }`, no default export) that registers
model-facing tools through `ctx.tools.register`.

It exposes **one tool surface**: 26 hand-written tools over the **Linear GraphQL
API** (`https://api
.linear.app/graphql`), authenticated with a personal API token.

**There is no MCP in this package — at all.** It does not host an MCP server, it
does not act as an

MCP client, it never connects to `mcp.linear.app`, and it has
no MCP configuration, dependency, or t

est. The 26 `linear_*` tools below are the
entire surface; nothing else is registered under any cond

he 26 `linear_*` tools below are the
entire surface; nothing else is registered under any condition.

> **Scope honesty:** 25 of these tools are a fixed, hand-modelled subset of what
> the Linear GraphQ

L API can do. They cover issues, comments, relations, teams,
> states, labels, projects, cycles and

users — and nothing beyond that (no
> attachments, no documents/projects search, no webhooks, no aut

h/user-management
> administration, no bulk operations). The set is not auto-discovered and does not

> grow on its own: if you need a capability outside the table below, it is not
> there. The 26th to

ol, `linear_graphql`,
> is the deliberate escape hatch for exactly that case — but what it can reach

is
> bounded by Linear's own API and by your key's permissions, so it extends
> coverage, it does n
ot guarantee parity. See Limitations.

> Status: this is **version 0.2.5** of the standalone implementation — the
> GitHub release for it i

s
> KB1SLN-Labs/dsh-linear/releases/tag/v0.2.5,
> and the package is published on npm as `@kb1slnlab

s/dsh-linear`. **0.2.5** marks

## Tools
### GraphQL tools (`linear_*`) — 26 registrations
| Tool | Purpose |
| `linear_issue_list` | List issues (filter by team key, state name, free-text search; `limit` defau

lt 20, max 50; cursor pagination via `after` / `pageInfo`) |

### What is verified vs. what is not

- **Verified (mock-tested):** what `test.js` asserts — registration of exactly the 26
tools, GraphQL

query/mutation shape, the raw-key auth header form, identifier
resolution, `{ error }` payloads, cu

rsor pagination on all eight direct list
tools (first-page `pageInfo`, `after` passed only as a `$af

ter` variable, blank
and non-string cursors treated as no cursor, a bad cursor surfacing as a clean

error, and a pageInfo-less server normalising to `null`), page sizes unchanged
(`limit` default 20 c

lamped to max 50; `team_list` still `first: 100` with no
`limit` parameter),
the five direct write t

ools (`projectUpdate`, `commentUpdate`, `commentDelete`,
`issueArchive`, `issueUnarchive`) — includi

ng that an unresolved project name or issue
identifier never reaches a mutation and that a `success:

false` payload surfaces as a
clean error — the `linear_graphql` escape hatch (a query document and

a mutation
document forwarded verbatim, caller variables arriving as variables rather than query
tex

t, blank/non-string/missing `query` and non-object `variables` rejected before any
request, GraphQL

`errors[]` and non-2xx responses surfacing through the same
`{ error }` wrapper; all against loopbac

k, so no real write happens) — and that an
`mcp` config block is inert (registers nothing, logs noth

ing, calls no effect).
- **Verified against real host services (not mocks):** `test-loader.mjs` load

s this
package through the real plugin loader into a real `ToolRuntime`. The scratch profile
behind

that run was installed via the **DSH plugin manager** and verified on **desktop

o LLM turn, session log, sandbox, or app entry tree

## Limitations
Stated plainly, because 25 of the tools above are a fixed hand-modelled subset:

- **Pagination covers the list tools but not the page sizes.** All eight list
tools paginate (`after

` + `pageInfo`), so nothing is cut off *silently* — you can
always continue from `pageInfo.endCursor

`. What stays capped is the page size:
`limit` defaults to 20 and never exceeds **50** (`issue_list`

, `comment_list`,
`project_list`, `cycle_list`, `user_list`), while `team_list` sends a fixed
`first

: 100` and takes no `limit`, and `state_list`/`label_list` take no `limit`
at all. A single call the

refore returns only one capped page; reading everything
means following the cursor yourself. The `_g

et` tools are not paginated — they
fetch one entity.
- **No search beyond free-text on issues.** `li

near_issue_list`'s `search` matches
title/description case-insensitively; there is no project, docum

ent, or cycle search.
- **Create/update coverage is narrow but no longer empty.** Issues, comments,

relations,
labels and projects can be created; issues and projects can be updated, comments edited
a

nd deleted, and issues archived/unarchived. Nothing else can: there is no team or state
management,

no cycle create, no project delete, no bulk operation, no attachment upload,
and no user administrat

ion. Among the named tools, `linear_comment_delete` is the
only destructive one and has no undo — bu

t it is not the only destructive thing
this package can do: `linear_graphql` runs any mutation your

key permits, so
operations outside the named set (deletions included) are reachable through it.
- **

`linear_comment_add` targets issues only** — it sends `CommentCreateInput.issueId`,
so it cannot com

ment on a project, update, or document.
- **Fields are projected, not passed through.** The 25 named

tools return the fixed
field sets in the GraphQL fragments (e.g. an issue's state as a name string)

, so
anything not in those fragments is simply absent from the result. `linear_graphql`
passes `data

` through raw instead — which is why its coverage is whatever Linear's
API exposes, and nothing more

raw instead — which is why its coverage is whatever Linear's
API exposes, and nothing more.
